# The checks

**Generated by `tools/gen_checks.py` from `docs/checks.yaml` and a live run over 22 specs. Do not edit.**

Every example below is a real finding from a real spec in this repo, produced by running the
linter — not written by hand.

**Evidence column, and read it before quoting any rate:**

- **robust** — survived independent encoding by a model that had never seen this project
- measured — fires on the corpus; not separately checked against an independent encoder
- motivated — three real instances justify it; **not yet evidenced at rate**
- legacy — inherited from the general programme, never fires on agent loops

> Only two checks are `robust`. Everything else measured the person doing the encoding
> as much as it measured the corpus. That is the honest ceiling on current evidence, and
> it is why this is a notation first and a linter second.

## `regulator_without_model`

> *"it reacts but never anticipates"*

**What it looked at.** The loop steers toward a condition and contains no model — no `explains` — of what produces that quantity.

**How to fix it.** Add `explains:` to the belief that accounts for the goal, or accept that this is a reflex against a setpoint.

**Status.** fires on **22 of 22** specs here · **robust**. Conant & Ashby 1970 — every good regulator of a system must be a model of that system. 10/10 published examples. Survived independent encoding 5/5.

**Real finding**, from `examples/cascade.loop.yaml`:

> The loop regulates `target_cac` but contains no MODEL of it — no Explanation of what generates it. Conant & Ashby (1970): every good regulator of a system must be a model of that system. Without one this is a reflex against a setpoint, not a regulator, and it cannot anticipate.

---

## `belief_never_checked`

> *"my agent's confidence doesn't track reality"*

**What it looked at.** A belief formed by judgement, with no `checked_by` naming what scores it against outcomes.

**How to fix it.** Add `checked_by:` to the belief, naming what compares past calls to what happened. If nothing does, that is the finding.

**Status.** fires on **20 of 22** specs here · **robust** · the *calibration* half. 10/10 published reference examples, 4/4 eval harnesses. Survived independent encoding 5/5.

**Real finding**, from `examples/customer_acquisition.loop.yaml`:

> The loop forms a belief about `product_market_fit` by bayesian, and nothing ever scores it against what actually happened. Add `checked_by:` naming what compares past calls to outcomes. Until then its confidence is a number nobody has ever been graded on, and it can be confidently wrong forever.

---

## `no_human_at_all`

> *"it never asks me anything"*

**What it looked at.** The loop has decision rules and names no person — nobody approves, nobody is escalated to, nobody bears the cost.

**How to fix it.** Declare the person under `people:` with `loses_if_wrong`, and add `asks_human_when:`.

**Status.** fires on **15 of 22** specs here · measured · the *attention* half. 14/21 of the corpus. Encoder-dependent — reported as a pattern, not a rate.

**Real finding**, from `examples/cascade.loop.yaml`:

> The loop makes decisions — 2 rule(s) — and declares no person anywhere. Nobody approves anything, nobody is escalated to, and nobody is recorded as bearing the cost when it is wrong. Whatever this loop does, it does unattended and unowned.

---

## `unbounded_loop`

> *"it ran all weekend"*

**What it looked at.** The loop declares nothing it can run out of — no ceiling, no budget.

**How to fix it.** Declare it under `spends:` even if the limit is generous. An undeclared budget is still a budget, just one nobody chose.

**Status.** fires on **12 of 22** specs here · measured · the *attention* half. Harness engineering — budgets and step ceilings are standard practice. Fires 11/21.

**Real finding**, from `examples/cascade.loop.yaml`:

> The loop declares nothing it can run out of — no iteration ceiling, no token or time budget, no attention it spends. Nothing in the encoding says what stops it, so it runs until something outside reaches in and halts it. Declare it under `spends:` even if the limit is generous; an undeclared budget is still a budget, just one nobody chose.

---

## `no_exogenous_grounding`

> *"it confirms its own beliefs"*

**What it looked at.** Every observation the loop reads is `origin: ourselves` — produced inside the system.

**How to fix it.** Add at least one observation with `origin: outside`. Without one it converges on agreement rather than truth.

**Status.** fires on **9 of 22** specs here · measured · the *attention* half.

**Real finding**, from `examples/field/conviction_termination.loop.yaml`:

> Loop `conviction_termination` reads only ['resolved_hypotheses', 'scenario_probabilities'], and every one of those is produced by an act inside this group. Nothing it observes can surprise it. It cannot be wrong in a way it did not already contain, so it will converge on agreement rather than on truth.

---

## `unmeasured_estimand`

> *"it claims to track things it doesn't"*

**What it looked at.** A quantity with no observation informing it.

**How to fix it.** Add an entry to `observes:` with `informs:` pointing at it, or stop claiming to track it.

**Status.** fires on **9 of 22** specs here · measured · the *attention* half. Kalman observability — a state is observable if it can be inferred from outputs.

**Real finding**, from `examples/customer_acquisition.loop.yaml`:

> Estimand `payback_months` has no signal measuring it. Any estimate of it is formed from something the encoding does not record.

---

## `reinforcing_loop_no_balancer`

> *"it runs away"*

**What it looked at.** A loop whose links are all positive — nothing corrects it downward.

**How to fix it.** Add a balancing path, typically an exogenous measurement that can contradict the loop.

**Status.** fires on **7 of 22** specs here · measured. System dynamics loop polarity — Forrester, Sterman.

**Real finding**, from `examples/field/conviction_termination.loop.yaml`:

> Loop `conviction_termination` is REINFORCING: its signal `resolved_hypotheses` is produced by its own intervention, and no exogenous signal measures what it measures. System dynamics: a loop with no negative link diverges rather than self-corrects. Nothing outside the loop can contradict it.

---

## `ceiling_without_correction`

> *"it hit the wall and stopped, with no warning"*

**What it looked at.** A limit exists and no decision rule reads how much is left.

**How to fix it.** Have a rule in `when:` read the resource and do something different when it runs low. A ceiling is a stop, not a correction — it truncates the loop rather than regulating it.

**Status.** fires on **6 of 22** specs here · measured · the *attention* half. Ashby — a stop absorbs no disturbance. Known limit: this clears as soon as anything reads the resource, and does not distinguish reading-to-halt from reading-to-adapt.

**Real finding**, from `examples/field/ralph.loop.yaml`:

> `iterations` has a limit of `the hard iteration ceiling` and no decision rule reads how much is left. The loop runs at full rate until it hits the wall and stops. A ceiling is a stop, not a correction: it truncates the loop rather than regulating it, and the halt is indistinguishable from failure and arrives without warning. To regulate, some rule in `when:` has to read `iterations` and do something different when it runs low.

---

## `consequence_without_authority`

> *"I carry the risk and control none of it"*

**What it looked at.** A person bears a consequence and authorises no action.

**How to fix it.** Give them authority over something via `needs_approval:`, or record that the exposure is genuinely one-sided.

**Status.** fires on **6 of 22** specs here · measured.

**Real finding**, from `examples/customer_acquisition.loop.yaml`:

> `investor` bears consequence `investor_consequence` (severity `None`) and the encoding records no `authorizes` edge from it to any intervention.

---

## `irreversible_without_approval`

> *"my agent did something I can't undo"*

**What it looked at.** An action marked `can_undo: no` or `costly` with no `needs_approval`.

**How to fix it.** Add `needs_approval:` naming the person who must say yes. Approval demanded everywhere is ignored; approval where the act cannot be undone is a rule people follow.

**Status.** fires on **6 of 22** specs here · measured.

**Real finding**, from `examples/customer_acquisition.loop.yaml`:

> Intervention `exit_channel` is marked `irreversible` and declares no `requires_approval_from`. The loop may take an act it cannot undo with no human gate. This is the question every agent deployment turns on and no framework represents it.

---

## `single_point_of_grounding`

> *"everything rests on one input and nobody says so"*

**What it looked at.** The loop reads several observations and exactly one comes from outside itself.

**How to fix it.** Nothing to fix necessarily — but the loop is exactly as trustworthy as that one input. Ralph is the canonical case: weaken the tests and it is sealed.

**Status.** fires on **6 of 22** specs here · measured · the *attention* half.

**Real finding**, from `examples/field/meeseeks_sourcing.loop.yaml`:

> Loop `meeseeks_sourcing` reads 2 observations and exactly one of them — `published_research` — comes from outside itself. Everything else it looks at, it produced. `published_research` is therefore the only thing that can fail in a way this loop did not intend, and the loop is exactly as trustworthy as that one input. Weaken it and the loop is sealed.

## `informs_no_decision`

> *"I'm paying for information that changes nothing"*

**What it looked at.** An observation informs a belief, and no decision rule reads that belief. Sharper than `orphan_signal`, which catches informing *nothing*.

**How to fix it.** Either have a rule in `when:` read it, or stop observing it. The loop is not wrong about anything here — it is spending attention it will not get back.

**Status.** fires on **5 of 22** specs here · motivated · the *attention* half. Value of information, from decision theory. Fires 1/10 on published examples — motivated, not yet evidenced at rate.

**Real finding**, from `examples/cascade.loop.yaml`:

> `runway_model` is collected and tells you about `target_cac`, and no decision rule reads `target_cac`. The loop is not wrong about anything here — it is paying attention to something that changes nothing it does. Either a rule should read `target_cac`, or this observation should stop.

---

## `accountable_but_blind`

> *"I'm accountable for it and I find out afterwards"*

**What it looked at.** A person with `loses_if_wrong` and nothing in `sees` — bears the cost, receives no information.

**How to fix it.** Add estimands to that person's `sees:`, or move the exposure to whoever actually watches.

**Status.** fires on **4 of 22** specs here · measured · the *attention* half.

**Real finding**, from `examples/customer_acquisition.loop.yaml`:

> Party `investor` bears a consequence and holds no estimate — nothing in the loop routes information to them. They carry the cost of being wrong and receive nothing with which to be right. Human-in-the-loop in name only.

---

## `no_escalation_path`

> *"there is no point at which it stops and asks"*

**What it looked at.** A human is declared, and no rule escalates and no action needs approval.

**How to fix it.** Add `asks_human_when:` with the conditions that should stop the loop.

**Status.** fires on **4 of 22** specs here · measured · the *attention* half.

**Real finding**, from `examples/field/conviction_termination.loop.yaml`:

> The loop declares 1 part(ies) and 1 polic(ies), and no policy escalates and no intervention requires approval. There is no point at which this loop stops and asks. It either succeeds or fails silently.

---

## `spends_without_limit`

> *"it quietly runs out"*

**What it looked at.** Something consumed with no ceiling and nothing replenishing it.

**How to fix it.** Give it a `limit:`, or declare what `replenished:` it. Exhaustion is certain; only the date is unstated.

**Status.** fires on **4 of 22** specs here · measured · the *attention* half.

**Real finding**, from `examples/customer_acquisition.loop.yaml`:

> `increase_budget` consumes `runway`, and `runway` has no declared limit and nothing replenishes it. It only ever goes down, and the encoding does not say how far down it can go before this stops working. Exhaustion is certain; only the date is unstated.

---

## `expensive_signal_unreviewed`

> *"we keep paying for a source nobody asks about"*

**What it looked at.** An observation with `cost: high` or `medium` and no `checked_by` reviewing whether it earns that.

**How to fix it.** Add `checked_by:` to the observation — the way a sourcing channel that finds nothing gets retired.

**Status.** fires on **3 of 22** specs here · motivated · the *attention* half. Three independent instances in the corpus. Fires 3/21 — motivated, not evidenced at rate.

**Real finding**, from `examples/customer_acquisition.loop.yaml`:

> `customer_interviews` costs `high` to obtain and nothing reviews whether it earns that. Beliefs here get scored against outcomes; the SOURCES do not. Add `checked_by:` naming what asks whether looking here was worth it — the way a channel that finds nothing gets retired.

## `orphan_signal`

> *"it collects data nobody uses"*

**What it looked at.** An observation with no `informs:`.

**How to fix it.** Add `informs:` naming what it tells you, or stop collecting it.

**Status.** fires on **3 of 22** specs here · measured · the *attention* half.

**Real finding**, from `examples/customer_acquisition.loop.yaml`:

> Signal `board_sentiment` is observed but is not connected to any estimand. You are collecting it without having said what it tells you.

---

## `insufficient_variety`

> *"it can only do one thing and the world does many"*

**What it looked at.** More things named in `not_modelling` than there are distinguishable actions.

**How to fix it.** Name more levers, or accept that the loop cannot absorb what it has already listed. A crude proxy — Ashby's variety is a measure over states, not a headcount — so treat it as a prompt to think, not a proof.

**Status.** fires on **2 of 22** specs here · motivated. Ashby 1956, Law of Requisite Variety. Listed as blocked on a missing `Disturbance` primitive for most of the project; it was never blocked, because `not_modelling:` IS the disturbance list.

**Real finding**, from `examples/field/ralph.loop.yaml`:

> The loop declares 1 distinct action(s) — ['implement_one_task'] — and 2 thing(s) it is knowingly not modelling: ['token cost', 'whether the task was the right task']. Only variety can destroy variety: a regulator needs at least as many distinguishable responses as the disturbance has modes. Either name more levers, or accept that the loop cannot absorb what it has already listed.

---

## `policy_reads_undeclared`

> *"it branches on something that doesn't exist"*

**What it looked at.** A decision rule tests an identifier declared nowhere — not a goal, not a belief, not a resource.

**How to fix it.** Declare it, or fix the condition. Nothing observes it and nothing computes it, so whatever happens at that branch is not what the spec says.

**Status.** fires on **2 of 22** specs here · measured · the *calibration* half.

**Real finding**, from `examples/field/conviction_termination.loop.yaml`:

> The decision rule tests `avg_confidence`, and `avg_confidence` is declared nowhere in this loop — not as a goal, not as a belief. Nothing observes it and nothing computes it. The rule reads a quantity that does not exist, so whatever it does at that branch is not what the spec says it does.

---

## `shared_estimand_no_arbiter`

> *"my agents disagree and whichever finishes last wins"*

**What it looked at.** Two loops in a group estimate the same quantity and no policy reconciles them.

**How to fix it.** Have a rule read the quantity and decide, or make one loop's estimate authoritative.

**Status.** fires on **2 of 22** specs here · measured · the *calibration* half.

**Real finding**, from `examples/research_group.loop.yaml`:

> `claim_truth` is estimated by 2 independent estimators — ['verifier_estimate_claim_truth', 'worker_estimate_claim_truth'], by method(s) ['judgement'] — and no policy in the group reads it. When they disagree nothing reconciles them, so the value that survives is whichever wrote last. Felt symptom: my agents disagree and the answer depends on ordering.

---

## `uncontrollable_target`

> *"it has a goal it can't actually move"*

**What it looked at.** A goal with a target, and no action declaring it `moves` that quantity.

**How to fix it.** Add `moves:` to whichever action drives it. A target nothing can drive is a wish.

**Status.** fires on **2 of 22** specs here · measured. Kalman controllability — a state is controllable if it can be driven to a target.

**Real finding**, from `examples/field/ralph.loop.yaml`:

> `agent_says_done_target` sets a target on `agent_says_done`, and no intervention declares that it moves `agent_says_done`. Controllability: a target nothing can drive toward is a wish, not a setpoint. The loop declares 1 intervention(s) — ['implement_one_task'] — and none of them acts on this quantity.

---

## `unowned_act`

> *"two agents can do the same thing under different rules"*

**What it looked at.** One action selected by policies belonging to different loops.

**How to fix it.** Give the action one owner. Authority decided by scheduling is not authority.

**Status.** fires on **1 of 22** specs here · measured.

**Real finding**, from `examples/research_group.loop.yaml`:

> Intervention `emit_report` is selected by 2 policies — ['verifier_policy', 'worker_policy'] — belonging to different loops. Nothing says which one owns it, so its approval rule is whichever loop reaches it first. Authority decided by scheduling is not authority.

---

## `cascade_timescale_inversion`

> *"the two loops fight each other"*

**What it looked at.** A goal `set_by` another loop, where the inner loop runs no faster than the outer one.

**How to fix it.** Make the inner loop faster, or slow the outer one. In cascade control the inner loop must settle before the outer acts again — otherwise the outer corrects against a response that has not arrived and both hunt. Silent when either cadence cannot be ranked.

**Status.** fires on **0 of 22** specs here · motivated. Cascade control — a necessary condition, not a preference.

---

## `frozen_setpoint`

> *"the target has not changed in a year and nobody owns it"*

**What it looked at.** A goal `set_by: <loop>.<quantity>` where no action anywhere moves that quantity.

**How to fix it.** Give the outer loop an action that moves it, or stop claiming the target is managed. The hierarchy is drawn and the target never changes — the inner loop regulates against a constant an outer loop is nominally responsible for and never revisits.

**Status.** fires on **0 of 22** specs here · motivated. The failure `set_by` exists to make visible.

---

## `open_loop`

> *"it observes, and it acts, and the two are unrelated"*

**What it looked at.** The quantity is measured AND moved, and no loop closes between them.

**How to fix it.** Make sure the loop reading that signal is the one taking that action.

**Status.** fires on **0 of 22** specs here · measured.

---

## Legacy checks

Inherited from the general programme, before the fork to agent loops. None fires on the
current corpus. Kept because they are still correct for hand-written graph encodings, and
recorded here so nobody mistakes silence for coverage.

| check | why it is quiet |
|---|---|
| `estimand_never_estimated` | Subsumed by `unmeasured_estimand` and `uncontrollable_target` on the authoring path; unreachable because every belief gets an estimator by construction. Still live for hand-written graph encodings. |
| `estimate_without_authority` | A party holding an estimate that authorises no intervention. |
| `estimate_without_estimator` | An Estimate node with nothing estimating it. |
| `hinge_without_resolution` | A critical quantity with no resolution condition. |
| `hinge_without_sensor` | A critical quantity with no signal. |
| `interventions_without_policy` | Actions with no policy selecting them. |
| `invariant_on_unmeasured` | A constraint over a quantity nothing measures. |
| `measurement_authority_inversion` | The richest signal feeds a party that does not authorise the decisive act. |
| `no_loop_closed` | Parts declared and nothing closing. |
| `open_question_delay_exposure` | A delay whose exposure falls on a party who cannot act. |
| `policy_entirely_blind` | A policy none of whose inputs are measured. |
| `policy_on_unmeasured_inputs` | A rule reading a declared quantity nothing measures. |
| `uncalibrated_estimator` | Superseded by `belief_never_checked`. Required `criticality: existential`, a field the authoring format has no key for, which gated the project's headline finding behind something nobody could write. |
| `unowned_cross_timescale_coupling` | Loops at different timescales touching one object with no owner. |
